why_ai: Locksmiths open, rekey and repair locks and program keys by hand at doors and vehicles, licensed in 13 states and trusted with entry, though smart locks and kiosks erode the simplest mechanical work.
why_clarity: A door that opens or a key that turns is checked on the spot and lockouts and rekeys recur, but diagnosis of commercial openings varies and is judged later by callbacks.
why_digital: The input is a physical lock, door or vehicle, the work is done by hand on site, and customers find locksmiths through local search.

why_ai: Repairing closers, exit devices, locks and frames happens by hand at each opening, and facilities keep paying a trusted vendor for it.
why_clarity: Codes and hardware functions define the target, but every opening's fault differs and whether a fix held is known only weeks later.
why_digital: Tickets arrive digitally, but the work and the result are physical doors serviced by a local or regional vendor.

why_ai: A qualified person must physically check each fire door and fix deficiencies, though photo-based tools will speed the documentation.
why_clarity: NFPA 80 lists exactly what to check and the same assemblies recur, with pass or fail confirmed at the next survey.
why_digital: Starts from physical doors on site and ends in a report plus repairs, sold to local facilities.

why_ai: Fitting electrified locks and strikes that must satisfy egress and fire codes is hands-on, code-bound site work.
why_clarity: Schedules and codes define each door, but every project's combination differs, and commissioning gives a quick pass or fail.
why_digital: Starts from drawings and schedules but the installation and the result are physical, bought through project bids.

why_ai: Cutting and programming keys happens at the vehicle with NASTF credentials, though dealers and kiosks compete for simpler jobs.
why_clarity: A working key is an exact, instant result and jobs recur, but procedures vary by vehicle and tool.
why_digital: Security data and programmers are digital, but the vehicle and the key are physical and the job is bought locally.

why_ai: Pinning cylinders is manual and the client trusts whoever holds the system design, though the design itself is computable.
why_clarity: Bitting rules are codified and a key either opens a door or not, but each system is a one-off design maintained over decades.
why_digital: Charts and ledgers could be data, but cylinders are pinned by hand and the work is bought from a local locksmith.

why_ai: Opening and repairing safes by manipulation or precise drilling is rare craft work by trusted, vetted technicians.
why_clarity: An opened safe is an unambiguous result, but methods are personal and every lockout differs.
why_digital: The input is a physical container and the work is done by hand on site for local or regional clients.

why_ai: The owner-operator does physical lockouts, rekeys and car keys alone, and customers still need a person at the door.
why_clarity: Most jobs are routine with an immediate result, though pricing and verification rest on the owner's judgement.
why_digital: Physical work found through local search and delivered by hand from a van.

why_ai: Batch key programming still needs a technician at each vehicle, but the buyer treats it as a commodity line item.
why_clarity: Each unit needs a working key, the job repeats across lots of VINs, and success is known immediately.
why_digital: VIN lists are digital, but each key is cut and programmed at the vehicle for a local business buyer.

why_ai: Answering, quoting and dispatching a lockout is phone and screen work that voice agents can largely perform.
why_clarity: A quote honoured or not, a call converted or not, across thousands of near-identical calls.
why_digital: Calls and dispatch data are digital, but the outcome is a technician at a door, sold through online search.

why_ai: Mechanical rekeys need a technician, but smart locks are turning access resets into a remote code change.
why_clarity: Reset access at every turn is a clear, repeated task checked by whether old keys or codes still work.
why_digital: Work orders are digital, but most resets are still physical, bought by regional property managers.

why_ai: Reverse-engineering each new immobilizer is adversarial engineering that automakers keep changing, though it is screen and bench work.
why_clarity: Coverage either programs the car or not, but each vehicle generation needs fresh investigation.
why_digital: Vehicle protocols and firmware are the input, development is on screens and benches, and updates ship as software worldwide.

why_ai: Lead pricing, ranking and fraud detection are software and analyst work on platform data.
why_clarity: Leads, bookings and disputes are counted precisely at high volume, with fast feedback.
why_digital: Entirely digital marketplaces bought and used online.

why_ai: Category, pricing and supplier analytics run on the distributor's transaction data on screens, with some protection from supplier and account relationships.
why_clarity: Prices, margins and sell-through are measured exactly across thousands of repeat purchases, with results visible within a programme year.
why_digital: Purchase histories and catalogues in, price files and supplier reports out, all on screens, though buyers deal with a few known distributors.

why_ai: Locks are installed physically, but the platform's value is software that automation and standards commoditise.
why_clarity: Lock events and device health are logged precisely across many near-identical units.
why_digital: Device data in, cloud software out, sold to property managers through remote sales.

why_ai: A machine already scans and cuts the key; people only service kiosks.
why_clarity: A copied key works or not, millions of times, under a fixed procedure.
why_digital: A physical key goes in and a physical key comes out at a store kiosk.

why_ai: Testing security hardware and acting as the government's technical authority is accountable, hands-on and judgement-heavy work.
why_clarity: Specifications define pass and fail, but evaluations vary by product and field failures surface slowly.
why_digital: Mixes physical testing with written specifications and guidance delivered to installations remotely.

why_ai: Writing hardware schedules is document work that configurators and AI drafting can increasingly produce.
why_clarity: Schedules follow codified hardware functions and recur project by project, checked at submittal.
why_digital: Drawings in, schedules out, entirely on screens for architects anywhere.

why_ai: Application vetting and audits are rule-based screen work, though decisions carry security accountability.
why_clarity: Eligibility rules are written down and applications repeat, with clear approval outcomes.
why_digital: An online registry and portal used remotely by locksmiths and automakers.

why_ai: Training, certification and standards committees rely on member relationships more than on hands-on work.
why_clarity: Exams are defined, but standards and advocacy outcomes are slow and diffuse.
why_digital: Mostly documents, exams and events, with some in-person training.

why_ai: Franchisor work is marketing, call routing and support for local owners, much of it automatable.
why_clarity: Franchise operations repeat across territories, but success depends on many local factors.
why_digital: Call centres and marketing are digital while franchisees deliver physical service locally.

why_ai: Examining locks under magnification and testifying is accountable expert work that courts want a person to do.
why_clarity: Findings are argued case by case and confirmed, if ever, by a verdict.
why_digital: Starts from physical locks and keys and ends in reports and testimony bought through insurers and counsel.

why_ai: Compiling code tables is data work that automakers' own portals and software increasingly replace.
why_clarity: Codes map exactly to bittings, every lookup is identical in kind, and errors show immediately.
why_digital: Data in, software out, sold online.
